section.steps_2: Enter the characters or text you want to keep.
section.steps_3: Choose TTF, WOFF, or WOFF2 output.
section.steps_4: Click Start Compression and download the optimized font.
section.why_text: Large fonts increase page load time, especially on mobile devices or when multiple font files are used. Font compression and subsetting can significantly improve web performance and reduce download size.
section.faq_1_q: What is a font subsetting tool?
section.faq_1_a: A font subsetting tool keeps the characters you actually need and removes the rest to create a smaller font file.
section.faq_2_q: How do I reduce the size of a TTF file?

exifGuide.title: What is EXIF data?
exifGuide.description: Learn what EXIF can reveal, how it differs from other image metadata, and how to inspect or remove it before sharing photos.
exifGuide.whatBody: EXIF (Exchangeable Image File Format) is a set of metadata commonly embedded in photos by cameras and phones. It describes how an image was captured; it is separate from the visible pixels.
exifGuide.fieldsBody: Depending on the device and app, EXIF may include the capture date and time, camera or phone model, exposure settings, orientation, and GPS coordinates. Images can also contain other metadata formats such as IPTC or XMP.
exifGuide.viewBody: Viewing tools read the metadata that a file exposes and present available fields. Missing fields do not necessarily mean that a photo never had metadata; it may have been removed or unsupported.
exifGuide.editBody: Editing changes selected metadata fields. Support varies by file format and tool; this site's EXIF editor works with JPEG images.
exifGuide.removeBody: Removing metadata creates a new image copy. Re-encoding can also change image format or quality, so keep the original if you need it.
exifGuide.privacyBody: Location and capture details can reveal where or when a photo was taken. Check the actual output after cleanup, because apps and platforms may preserve, remove, or add metadata when exporting or sharing.
exifGuide.limitsBody: Metadata availability varies by file format and software. Removing EXIF does not remove information visible in the image itself, such as a street sign or face. Local processing means the selected file is handled in your browser; external features such as address lookup may send coordinates as described by that tool.
exifGuide.seoTitle: What Is EXIF? Image Metadata and Privacy Guide — OnliTool
exifGuide.seoDescription: Understand EXIF photo metadata, common fields such as GPS and camera details, and ways to inspect, edit, or remove metadata.

compressFontTarget.title: Compress {format} Online
compressFontTarget.description: Shrink {format} files by subsetting the glyphs you do not use and exporting an efficient web format. Everything runs locally in your browser.
compressFontTarget.whyDescription: Smaller font files mean faster page loads and better Core Web Vitals. Subset a font to the characters your site actually uses and ship a fraction of the original size.
compressFontTarget.question1: How do I compress a {format} file?
compressFontTarget.answer1: Open the font compressor, upload your {format} file, keep the characters you need and download a smaller web font. No file is uploaded to a server — it runs in your browser.
compressFontTarget.answer2: The glyphs you keep are untouched. The size saving comes from dropping the glyphs, ligatures and OpenType features your text never uses.
compressFontTarget.question3: Which output format should I choose?
compressFontTarget.answer3: WOFF2 is the best default for modern browsers; WOFF covers older ones. Always keep the original file for future edits.
compressFontTarget.seoDescription: Compress {format} files online by subsetting unused glyphs. Reduce font file size for the web without uploading — runs locally in your browser.
compressFontTarget.seoKeywords: compress {format}, {format} compressor, reduce {format} file size, {format} file compressor online, web font compression

fontSubset.whyDescription: A full CJK or icon font can weigh several megabytes; a subset containing the glyphs you actually use often lands in the low tens of kilobytes.
fontSubset.question1: How do I subset a font?
fontSubset.answer1: Paste the text your page renders (or pick a language preset), upload the font, and download the subset. Everything runs in your browser.
fontSubset.answer2: TTF, OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 inputs, with TTF, WOFF or WOFF2 output.
fontSubset.question3: Can a subset regain removed glyphs?
fontSubset.answer3: No. Keep the original font file — subsets permanently drop the characters that were not selected.

fontConvert.lead: Convert TTF, OTF and WOFF fonts to WOFF2 — or WOFF2 back to TTF — right in your browser. No upload, no account.
fontConvert.error: Conversion failed. The font may use unsupported tables or contain invalid data.
fontConvert.noFile: Choose a TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2 font file first.
fontConvert.localProcessing: The font never leaves your browser — conversion runs locally via WebAssembly.
fontConvert.q1: How do I convert TTF to WOFF2?
fontConvert.a1: Upload the TTF file, choose WOFF2 as the output and click Convert. The download starts immediately and nothing is sent to a server.
fontConvert.q2: Can I convert WOFF2 back to TTF?
fontConvert.a2: Yes. Pick TTF as the output format — the tool decompresses WOFF2 and rebuilds a standard TrueType font.
fontConvert.q3: Why is WOFF2 smaller than TTF?
fontConvert.a3: WOFF2 applies Brotli compression and a transform that packs glyph data more efficiently, typically cutting file size by another 30–50% compared with WOFF.
fontConvert.a4: Every modern browser since 2016 supports WOFF2. Serve TTF as a fallback only for very old devices.

mergeTool.faq1Q: How do I merge images into one image?
mergeTool.faq1A: Add two or more images, choose a layout (vertical, side by side or grid), adjust spacing and background, then click Merge images and download the result. Everything runs in your browser.
mergeTool.faq2Q: Can I merge screenshots without losing quality?
mergeTool.faq2A: Yes. Choose the vertical layout and the “Keep original pixels” strategy. Every screenshot is drawn at its native resolution with zero resampling, and the canvas grows to fit the stack.
mergeTool.faq3Q: Is there a limit on the number of images or file size?
mergeTool.faq3A: You can merge up to 20 images at once, with a 50-megapixel limit per image and a 200-megapixel total limit. Very large canvases are scaled down automatically and the tool shows the final size.
mergeTool.faq4A: Not when you export PNG or lossless WebP and keep the original-pixel strategy. JPG re-encodes the result, so use a high quality value if the merged image contains text or screenshots.
mergeTool.faq5Q: Can I control the final file size?
mergeTool.faq5A: You see the real encoded size before downloading. If the merged image is too heavy, the “Compress to a target size” button sends it to the image compressor with your target in kilobytes.
mergeTool.faq6Q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
mergeTool.faq6A: No. The merger uses the HTML canvas API inside your browser. Your files never leave your device, and there is no sign-up or watermark.
mergeTool.faq7Q: What is the difference between merging and a collage?
mergeTool.faq7A: Merging joins images edge to edge into one continuous picture. A collage arranges them in a template with overlaps and decorations. This tool focuses on clean merging, which is what screenshots, receipts and long charts need.
mergeTool.faq8Q: Can I merge images on iPhone or Android?
mergeTool.faq8A: Yes. Open this page in Safari or Chrome, choose photos from your gallery, and the merge happens on the device. HEIC photos should be converted to JPG first.
